- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reverting trend.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative; add 2–5% bias upward for first 5–7 days.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price dropping >3% from peak), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2% downward bias for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently 0.00, model exhibits high variance; use 30d moving average as baseline and apply ±1% smoothing to reduce overfitting.
